summary: Restore the zero-violation source dependency baseline without weakening architecture gates.
rationale: Public source failure interpretation was owned by the concrete Liepin source package, forcing runtime, runtime control, Workbench, UI, and source contracts to depend on a source implementation. The same inversion exposed the Liepin provider worker exception directly to Workbench v2. This change moves the shared product policy to an explicit neutral module, introduces a source-neutral worker error contract, and migrates every production consumer in one bounded compatibility-preserving slice.
dependency_rationale: Tach explicitly models the new stable failure-interpretation boundary and the consumers that are allowed to depend on it; the baseline remains empty and no forbidden dependency is accepted.
verification: uv run --group dev ruff check src tests experiments tools
uv run --group dev ty check src tests tools
deletion_targets: Runtime and product surfaces importing concrete Liepin failure-policy code
Workbench v2 catching a concrete Liepin provider exception
Runtime branching on the concrete Liepin source id to publish failure causes
risks: The compatibility module must remain a pure re-export so new production imports do not drift back to the concrete source package.
Failure causes must remain source-scoped so one source cannot publish another source's diagnostic codes.
Moving policy ownership must not change public problem codes, messages, user actions, or retry authority.
